events: # TableRows/1 as CSV. docs/reference.md, "Shared fixtures", defines the
#   events    JSON array, read RAW (no escape codec): {"schema":[labels]},
#             {"row":[cells]} and "end", fed in order. A cell is null,
#   options   JSON object, read RAW; empty is {}. Fields: delimiter (one
#             null_text (string), missing (string, or null for the error
#   expected  the exact output text through the escape codec (\r, \n, \t
#             and \\ decoded), or ERROR:<CODE> for the first failure.
# The standard profile (RFC 4180, always quoted, CRLF): Appendix A.
# Numbers: a lexeme is written as it is; a value alone takes the shortest form.
# A lexeme that is not a JSON number is INVALID_NUMBER.
# NaN and infinity have no CSV form, with or without a lexeme beside them.
# The lexeme is judged before the value: NaN spelled "NaN" is a bad lexeme.
# Null writes null_text, empty by default.
# Missing is MISSING_VALUE unless a text is configured; the text is quoted like any field.
# A row is checked whole before it is written: the first failing cell's code, wherever it is.
# Labels: duplicates allowed, quoted like fields; no rows still writes the header.
# The header can be turned off; every record, the last included, ends with the newline.
# Text is written as rows arrive; a table with no end is the records so far.
# Dialects: LF, other delimiters, minimal quoting.
# The quote, a line break and NUL cannot be the delimiter: refused when the renderer is built.
# A table with no columns has no CSV form.
# Protocol order: one schema, first; rows of its width; one end, last.
# Width is checked before cells: a short row holding Missing is a protocol error.
